title: A few of you asked how I made the guns, so here's the whole pipeline
author: Ditex_Design
selftext:
. I've built them three times, each a completely different way.

**V1: written in code.** No models at all. Each gun was one line of numbers (body size, barrel size, magazine size) and a handful of calls that each place one box. Eight boxes made a rifle. Every gun used the same boxes with different sizes, which is why they all looked alike.

**V2: built cube by cube.** Real shapes this time, 13 to 36 cubes per gun in four flat colours. I started in Blockbench, then moved to a script that generates the cube layouts, because placing them one at a time was too slow for a whole pack.

**V3: generated with Meshy.** This is what's in the game now.

1. One concept image per gun, based on my own 12-gun weapon sheet.
2. Image to 3D in Meshy.
3. Remesh down to about 10k triangles so it runs in a browser.
4. Export with 2K textures.

It costs 35 Meshy credits per gun (30 to generate, 5 to remesh), and I ran the same steps 12 times.

What I learned: the concept image matters most. My first try used a small crop from the sheet and the texture came out messy. Bigger, cleaner single-gun images fixed it.

BLOCKRIFT is a fast arena FPS that runs in the browser, coming soon at blockrift.io. Happy to answer anything about the workflow.
